## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Animal husbandry — breeds and management

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

**Animal husbandry** is the scientific management of livestock — cattle, poultry, fish (pisciculture), bees (apiculture) — for food and products. Modern strategies: improved breeds by **cross-breeding** (e.g. the sunflower-in-chapter example of Karan Swiss cattle), better feed and housing, disease control, and managed fisheries and apiculture. The goal is more milk, eggs, meat and honey per animal with less loss to disease.

**Concept flow — the branches of animal husbandry (study in this order)**

| Step | Branch | Product / aim |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dairy farm management | Milk: select high-yield breeds, good feed, clean housing, disease control |
| 2 | Poultry farm management | Eggs and meat: cross-bred layers and broilers, temperature-controlled housing |
| 3 | Pisciculture (fish farming) | Fish protein: managed ponds, hatcheries, composite fish culture |
| 4 | Apiculture (beekeeping) | Honey and wax: bee species, apiary siting, flowering seasons |
| 5 | Cross-breeding programmes | Superior breeds combining exotic yield with local hardiness |

**Livestock breeds and breeding — the classic examples**

| Animal | Local breed (hardy) | Exotic breed (high yield) | Cross / result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cattle | Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Gir | Holstein-Friesian, Brown Swiss, Jersey | Karan Swiss, Karan Fries — high milk yield with disease and heat tolerance |
| Poultry | Indigenous desi fowl | White Leghorn | Improved layers and broilers with high egg/meat output |
| Fish | Local major carps | — | Composite fish culture: 5–6 species with different feeding zones share one pond |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — why Karan Swiss works in Nepal's climate.** Pure Holstein-Friesian cows give 20+ litres a day in Europe but wilt in South Asian heat and succumb to local diseases. The local Sahiwal survives both but gives ~5 litres. Cross them and select: Karan Swiss combines the exotic milk yield with the local tolerance for heat, disease and coarse feed. The same logic produced Karan Fries and the improved poultry lines — breed for the environment, not just for the record book.

(3) Why cross-breed at all (yield vs hardiness)? (4) Explain composite fish culture and why it raises yield. (5) What is apiculture and what two products come from it?

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Branches in one line each: dairy (milk), poultry (eggs/meat), apiculture (bees/honey), pisciculture (fish), sericulture (silk) — five branches with products.
Trick 2: Cattle breeds: exotic high-yield (Jersey, Holstein-Friesian) vs indigenous hardy (Sahiwal, Gir, Red Sindhi); cross-breeding combines both — the two-column answer.
Trick 3: Poultry breeds: layers vs broilers; improved breeds need feed, hygiene, vaccination — management triad.
Trick 4: Bee-keeping: Apis indica common; Italian bee A. mellifera high honey yield; apiary location near flowers — the apiculture specifics.
